Plot iteration

Species richness vs survey year by substrate grouping, adjusted with feedback. Alignment of x-axes by column couldn’t be done but could be tried again in the future.

Exploring breeding period (April-July)

Mean species abundance vs survey year per substrate by time range. The set time ranges were chosen as four-month intervals based on the April-July potential breeding period. Specifically, the summer-fall range includes August through November and the winter-spring range includes January through March and December. I thought that this might be an interesting way to visualize whether certain substrates recorded more bird activity, comparing the four-month breednig period window to two other four-month ranges. A by month visualization may be more informative.

Analysis of species abundance by guild over varying measures of time. Top: Species abundance vs survey year by guild. Middle: Average species abundance vs season by guild. Bottom: Species abundance vs survey year brpken up by incremental seasons by guild. The bottom visualization accounting for individual seasons per survey year is a development of the top visualization, revealing more specific trends pertaining to seasons. I thought that it was difficult to differentiate the specific data points in the bottom plot following adjustment for seasons, inspiring a later visualization.

Analysis of species richness by guild over varying measures of time, like what was done with abundance. Top: Species richness vs survey year by guild. Middle: Average species richness vs season by guild. Bottom: Species richness vs survey year broken up by incremental seasons by guild. Like with abundance, I thought that the full effect of the survey year accounting for seasons would be best illustrated with an enlarged plot focusing on less, or just one, guild. Note that cormorants and kingfishers only record one species. They could be removed.

‘Waterfowl and Friends’ guild analysis. Top: Species abundance vs survey year and season. Bottom: Species richness vs survey year and season. With a larger plot, the season-specific changes become more obvious. Both plots conclude that species within the Waterfowl and Friends guild prefer the summer season and dislike the winter season. Since the summer season is defined by the month range from June to August in the current bird survey data aggregation, the abundance increase in the summer and decrease in the winter could be an iindicator of utilization of NCOS for breeding?
